newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes mostly firmer in consolidation.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes mostly firmer in consolidation.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed mostly firmer as the market attempted to consolidate following a steep slide Tuesday to a six-week low in the new crop July contract, traders said.
The market found support on news Egypt overnight bought 400,000 tonnes of U.S. soft red winter wheat and was seeking another 50,000 tonnes of U.S., French or Australian wheat.
"Wheat got early encouragement from the 400,000 tonnes purchased by Egypt," said Jerry Gidel, analyst for Dean Witter.
"But forecasts for some rain in the hard red winter wheat areas limited the enthusiasm after the initial pop," he said.
Meteorologists this week said rain was likely soon in Kansas and Nebraska.
Technical traders cited short term bullish signals from the nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for the July at roughly 31 percent, an oversold level.
But longer term, the July contract needs to drop to near $3.73 per bushel, the bottom of a chart gap set on April 7, chartists said.
CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed 1-3/4 cents per bushel higher to 1-1/2 lower, with July up 1-3/4 at $3.82-1/4.
